name: Context Effect
description: Memory retrieval improves when the cues present at recall match the environment or context in which information was learned. What people remember is partly shaped by where and under what conditions they encoded it, not just by the content itself.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to return-to-task experiences, just-in-time reminders, learning flows, saved drafts, and continuity cues; interfaces can make retrieval easier when they preserve or recreate the same context in which a task or piece of information was first learned.
myth_risk_note: A 2021 direct replication of the field's single most famous demonstration (Godden & Baddeley's underwater/land diving study) failed to find the classic same-context recall advantage. This doesn't overturn the broader environmental-context-dependent-memory literature (Smith & Vela's 2001 meta-analysis covers many other paradigms), but it is a real, citable failure to replicate the flagship study specifically -- worth flagging to anyone citing the diving study by name as if it were an unquestioned classic.
prevalence_note: Known in memory, learning, and context-aware product discussions, but rarely taught as a named first-tier UX law in mainstream interface-design practice.

findings.description: A direct replication of Godden & Baddeley's (1975) classic underwater/land context-dependent-memory demonstration, using the identical 2x2 within-subjects diver paradigm, did NOT find the classic same-context recall advantage -- contrary to the original study. An honest, real complication to the flagship demonstration of environmental context-dependent memory, though the broader effect (per Smith & Vela's 2001 meta-analysis across many other paradigms) remains well-supported; this specific diving paradigm's robustness is now genuinely in question.
findings.source_title: The Godden and Baddeley (1975) experiment on context-dependent memory on land and underwater: a replication

findings.description: A review and meta-analysis concluded that memory retrieval can improve when the original environmental context is reinstated at test, supporting context-dependent memory as a real if condition-sensitive retrieval effect.
findings.source_title: Environmental context-dependent memory: A review and meta-analysis
